why: The VNB figures (up 61% to Rs 3,136 crore, margin 22.9% from 15.4%) and the 'higher investment income' driver come from the part of the IANS piece that recaps the PREVIOUS quarter (the paragraph starting 'Meanwhile, in previous quarter... Rs 13,492 crore'). They are not stated for July-September. The 15.4% base matches LIC's April-June 2025 VNB margin, which points to these being April-June 2026 figures. IANS says the Q2 profit was 'driven by growth in premium collections and an improvement in asset quality'. The standfirst, the third key point, the 'New policies earn more' section, the closing 'main drivers' line, the infographic VNB stat, the SEO description and the Hindi twin all repeat the misattributed numbers.
